process_summary: The diagram shows a fruit-and-cheese plate assembly cell with an upper ingredient/loading area, a shared robotic manipulation zone, and two parallel rows of trays in the lower assembly/inspection area. Operators O1 and O2 load the upper area; operators O3 and O4 are associated with the finished-product end. Inputs are three cheese varieties, grapes, apples, wrapped crackers, empty plastic trays, and separate clear lids. Trays are dispensed individually, filled, inspected by camera, closed with lids, and passed to finished-product staging. Inspection or closure failures go to reject/rework. Target output is 200 acceptable plates/hour. The ingredient supply formats are explicitly assumptions in the document, not confirmed supplier specifications.

process_steps.name: Operator loading and replenishment
process_steps.description: A common upper loading space labeled for O1 and O2 serves the cracker, three-cheese, apple, grape, and lid supply areas. Incoming bulk cases, cartons, and bags are described in the input table; unpacking methods are not shown.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Green upper band labeled 'operator loading space (O1; O2)' spanning the ingredient and lid stations.

process_steps.name: Cracker presentation
process_steps.description: Individually wrapped cracker packets, supplied stacked in cases, are presented on a conveyor belt toward the robotic manipulation zone.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Upper-left station labeled 'crackers' with packet-like rectangles, a downward arrow, and 'conveyor belt'; input table specifies individually wrapped packets.

process_steps.name: Three-variety cheese presentation
process_steps.description: Three separate cheese supply positions are retained. The first illustrated cheese stream is associated with 'linear feed w/ vibration'; adjacent streams are labeled '2nd cheese' and '3rd cheese'. The written reference plate has five cheese pieces: two Tillamook Sharp Cheddar, two Beecher's Flagship, and one brie wedge. Inputs are assumed to be three separately packed varieties of consistently pre-cut wedges.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Three adjacent cheese positions between crackers and apples; explanatory text specifies the five-piece, three-variety cheese composition.

process_steps.name: Apple presentation
process_steps.description: A separate apple supply station presents pre-sliced apples from refrigerated bulk bags to the robotic zone. Its feeding mechanism is not identified.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Dedicated pink column labeled 'apples'; input table specifies pre-sliced, refrigerated bulk bags.

process_steps.name: Grape presentation
process_steps.description: A separate grape supply station presents pre-portioned stemmed bunches from bulk cartons to the robotic zone. Its feeding mechanism is not identified.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Dedicated purple column labeled 'grapes'; input table specifies pre-portioned stemmed bunches in bulk cartons.

process_steps.name: Empty tray dispensing and presentation
process_steps.description: Nested plastic trays arrive in bulk cases. A magazine beside the lower assembly area is labeled for dispensing boxes one at a time. The lower area depicts two parallel rows, each with three empty tray/box positions before inspection. A separate downward 'boxes' arrow appears at the far left; its precise connection to the magazine is not drawn.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Left-side box magazine and downward 'boxes' arrow; six brown empty rectangles in two rows of three; input table identifies empty trays as nested plastic trays.

process_steps.name: Robotic plate assembly
process_steps.description: The shared robotic manipulation zone interfaces with the ingredient presentation stations and the two-row tray area. Plates receive cheese, grapes, apples, and wrapped crackers. Robot count, allocation of work between tray positions, and the transport mechanism are not shown.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Blue horizontal band labeled 'Robotic manipulation zone' above the lower tray area; rightward arrows lead from the empty-tray rows to filled plates.

process_steps.name: Camera inspection
process_steps.description: Filled plates are visually inspected for assembly completeness in both depicted rows. Passing plates move right toward closure; failing plates are routed to reject/rework.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: 'INSPECT w/ CAMERA' above one filled-plate position in each row, green rightward 'PASS' flow, and a red 'FAIL' arrow toward reject/rework.

process_steps.name: Lid supply and plate closure
process_steps.description: Separately supplied nested clear lids are presented at the upper-right lid station. Following inspection, plates are closed with lids. The rightmost plate in each row has an additional outline consistent with closure, but the closure actuator and verification method are not specified.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Upper-right stack labeled 'lids'; two double-outlined filled plates after the inspection pass arrows; output text explicitly states plates are closed with lids.

process_steps.name: Accepted-product handoff
process_steps.description: Acceptable closed plates pass rightward to the operator end labeled O3 and O4 and are transferred to finished-product staging. Required output is 200 acceptable plates/hour across the cell, not per depicted row.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Right-side 'operator end (O3; O4)' with green 'PASS' arrow; output paragraph identifies finished-product staging and target throughput.

process_steps.name: Reject and rework routing
process_steps.description: Failures from inspection and the downstream closure/output area go to reject/rework. The drawing does not identify a re-entry point or a rework station.
process_steps.diagram_evidence: Two red 'FAIL' arrows lead toward 'reject, goes back into rework'; written outputs include failures of inspection or closure.

clarification_questions.question: Can you confirm the assumed input formats and provide ingredient, tray, lid, and cracker-packet specifications or samples, including dimensions, weights, variability, cheese wrapping status, and portions per plate? Is the stated 2+2+1 cheese recipe the required production recipe?
clarification_questions.why_critical: These determine feeder feasibility, gripping, tray denesting, closure compatibility, vision checks, and cycle time.

clarification_questions.question: What are the ambient temperature and humidity, incoming ingredient temperatures, allowable out-of-refrigeration times, and any required temperature control at the presentation and assembly stations?
clarification_questions.why_critical: Cold-chain limits, condensation, and ingredient adhesion affect food safety, materials, sensors, and handling performance.

clarification_questions.question: Which equipment surfaces will directly contact exposed food, and what cleaning regime is required: dry cleaning, wipe-down, or washdown? Specify cleaning chemicals, concentrations, temperatures, spray pressure, and allergen-changeover requirements.
clarification_questions.why_critical: These establish food-contact material requirements, hygienic design, corrosion resistance, ingress protection, and cleanability.

clarification_questions.question: Is 200 acceptable plates/hour a sustained net rate including replenishment, rejects, cleaning, and downtime? What shifts, availability target, expected reject rate, peak rate, and product changeovers must the cell support?
clarification_questions.why_critical: Net output alone does not establish the gross equipment rate, robot count, feeder capacity, or duty rating.

clarification_questions.question: Are the two lower rows independently operated lanes or another arrangement of tray positions? Does vibratory feeding apply to all three cheese varieties? Which loading, lid placement, closure, rejection, and rework tasks belong to O1–O4 versus purchased automation?
clarification_questions.why_critical: The drawn stations can be preserved, but equipment quantities and integration scope cannot be finalized without their operating relationships and task allocation.

clarification_questions.question: What must inspection accept or reject, with what tolerances and false-accept/false-reject limits? What is the lid closure type, required closure force or process, and method for verifying closure?
clarification_questions.why_critical: These determine vision capability, closure tooling, detection hardware, and reject controls.

clarification_questions.question: What electrical supply, compressed-air pressure/flow/quality, vacuum, water, drainage, and control-network connections are available? What footprint, access, and installation constraints apply to the drawn arrangement?
clarification_questions.why_critical: Utilities and site limits determine compatible drives, pneumatics, cleaning provisions, and physical equipment sizing.

clarification_questions.question: Where will the cell be installed, and which food-contact, machinery safety, electrical, sanitation, and customer or airline certifications are mandatory? Will operators access the robotic zone during operation or replenishment?
clarification_questions.why_critical: Jurisdiction and access requirements determine applicable conformity obligations, component approvals, and safeguarding.

clarification_questions.question: How are failed plates removed, held, reworked, and returned, and what purchased equipment is required at the O3/O4 finished-product handoff?
clarification_questions.why_critical: The diagram defines these routes but not their devices, capacity, return interface, or supply boundaries.

extraction_uncertainties: The input table explicitly describes assumed supply formats; these should not be treated as verified supplier capabilities.
The cheese recipe is derived by the document author from a reference plate that 'appears to match' an airline platter; production confirmation is needed.
The handwritten magazine annotation appears to mean 'Magazine for boxes dispensed 1 at a time'; the drawing uses 'boxes' while the input table uses 'trays'. Their equivalence is not explicit.
The first cheese stream lacks a clear variety label. '2nd cheese' and '3rd cheese' identify adjacent streams, but no stream is mapped to a named variety.
The 'linear feed w/ vibration' annotation points toward the first cheese presentation area; it does not clearly specify identical feeder mechanisms for all three varieties.
The lower diagram clearly depicts two parallel rows, but does not establish independent conveyor lanes, indexing logic, or equipment count.
Six empty tray symbols, two inspection-stage filled plates, and two downstream outlined plates are drawn; these are depicted positions or states, not confirmed machine quantities or capacities.
The robotic zone does not specify robot count, end effectors, or whether lid handling is performed by the same robotic system.
Camera inspection is explicit, but camera count, lighting, inspection criteria, and closure-verification hardware are not shown.
The downstream double outlines are consistent with lidded plates, supported by the written output description; the actual closing mechanism is absent.
O1 and O2 are assigned to the loading space and O3 and O4 to the operator end. Detailed individual duties are not stated.
The reject/rework destination is explicit, but no return connection, re-entry station, or rework equipment is drawn.
No cutting, slicing, grape portioning, or cracker unwrapping station is shown; none has been added to the equipment extraction.
